findings.summary: SA-2 regex is over-narrow vs project's description-writing style
findings.detail: Tested TRIGGER_PATTERNS regex (\buse\s+(?:when|for)\b, \bwhen\s+\w+ing\b, \bdelegate\b, \bcalled?\s+when\b, \binvoke\s+when\b) against 10 of 29 flagged descriptions. Zero matches. All 10 descriptions DO communicate when-to-invoke ('At the X stage…', 'during per-layer Design', 'One invocation per …', 'Use at pipeline start') — none use the literal phrases the regex demands. Regex over-narrowness, not description quality. Tighter regex covering project conventions would fix 27-29 findings with one edit.
findings.resolution: Carries to Plan stage's U-2 decision; codebase evidence supports option (ii) — tighten regex. The 1-2 descriptions that may genuinely need rewriting are an edge case.

findings.summary: Category E bypass-approval BLOCKERs are auditor false positives
findings.detail: All 3 'Body instructs subagent to bypass approval/safety prompts' BLOCKERs fire on NEGATIVE instructions: 'You do NOT skip the permission policy', 'You do NOT skip the convergence check'. The auditor regex \b(ignore|bypass|skip|override)\b.{0,30}(approval|prompt|permission|safety|check)\b does not recognize negation; it matches the verb+noun pair regardless of preceding 'NOT'. These are guardrails, not bypasses.
findings.resolution: Surfaced 2026-05-21T17:55; SURFACING NOTE — this changes Category E's character: 3 of 6 are AUDITOR defects, not agent defects. PRD AC-FR-5-b (BLOCKER finding rate → 0) is satisfiable by either (i) reword negative instructions (less clear) OR (ii) tighten auditor regex to handle negation (better). Plan stage decision. The 3 wildcard-shell findings remain genuine agent defects.
